decisions.question: How does the core write SSE events sent on the handler thread before the drain loop starts, given HttpExchange.eventStream returns nothing and StreamDrain.drain is the only stream hand-over (r4 W2-001, W2-001 one default method)?
options: A: add-only default StreamDrain.attach(OutputStream) called by eventStream before it returns (deviation from W2-001 'one default method')
B: unbounded pre-drain buffer, no SPI change (deviation from r4 W2-001, conflicts I-012)
C: bounded queue with overflow (reverses r4 W2-001)
decisions.decision: A: add-only `default void attach(OutputStream out) {}` on StreamDrain; every adapter's eventStream calls drain.attach(out) with the exchange-synchronized body stream before returning; an adapter that never calls attach falls back to queuing; recorded as a deviation from the W2-001 'one default method' wording
decisions.rule: 3-member committee, sequential, stopped after 2 agreeing votes
